title: MRI machine-learning classifier estimates brain arteriolosclerosis in living older adults
summary: A machine-learning classifier using white matter hyperintensity, diffusion anisotropy and demographic features was first developed on ex-vivo MRI and autopsy pathology from 119 participants (AUC 0.78) and then translated to in-vivo MRI as ARTS. In a separate group of 79 mostly dementia-free participants ARTS had AUC 0.79, and higher scores predicted cognitive decline; replication used further cohorts of 72 and 244 participants. The AUC is modest and the pathology reference comes from autopsy.
ai_technology: Machine learning classifier on MRI-derived white matter and diffusion features

evidence.tested: Testing in a separate group of 79 participants against autopsy-based ground truth, with replication in two other cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Performance in more diverse populations and clinical utility; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A machine learning classifier scored the likelihood of arteriolosclerosis from MRI.
